title: Ea with claude
author: zavrl11
selftext:
Hello,

I would like to build an EA based on the ICT strategy. Has anyone managed to create an ICT EA that isn’t overfitted?  
I’m currently developing my own EA with Claude’s help, but I think I’ve made it too restrictive. In a two-year backtest, it only takes about 120 trades, yet it shows a profit of over $50,000. 

What strategy or approach do you use when building an ICT EA?

comments.author: Suitable_Tank
comments.body: Tried this since years, even reversed engineered trades etc. Did not work

comments.author: PoggiSlice
comments.body: Check your confluence. If there's too many then it's restricting your trade count unless you want 60 trades a year.

comments.author: roztok_potok
comments.body: Not worth it. You won't get positive results.

comments.author: Good_Character_20
comments.body: Quickest check on that 50k before anything else. Sort the trades by P&L, drop the top five, and see what is left. On 120 trades a single big move can be most of the result, and ICT setups tend to fire around exactly the kind of expansion that produces those. If the edge survives losing five trades out of 120, you have something worth developing. If it does not, everything else you tune is noise. The restrictiveness is probably not your problem. The problem is that every threshold you had to invent to make ICT mechanical, how many pips counts as a gap, how many bars for the sweep, what qualifies as displacement, is a free parameter. Twenty of those searched against one two year window will find something that looks brilliant whether or not anything is there.
